title: Viktor Frankl and the Space to Choose
short_teaser: Psychiatrist Viktor Frankl survived Nazi concentration camps and later wrote about the importance of meaning and inner choice under conditions of extreme suffering.
story: Psychiatrist Viktor Frankl survived Nazi concentration camps and later wrote about the importance of meaning and inner choice under conditions of extreme suffering. His work did not deny pain; it examined what human beings may still protect within themselves. Even when circumstances narrow our options, the way we relate to the moment can still matter. A person’s story becomes useful when it helps us recognize choices, courage, persistence, and possibility in our own life. The lasting value is not merely knowing the fact. It is seeing the pattern beneath it and considering where that same pattern may already be present in ordinary life, creative work, or business.
